newsitem.title: UK: Britain launches urgent inquiry into alcopops.
newsitem.headline: Britain launches urgent inquiry into alcopops.

text.p: British Home Secretary (interior minister) Jack Straw said on Friday he had asked for an urgent inquiry into the consumption of alcoholic lemonades and sodas known as alcopops.

"The Government is deeply concerned about the issues surrounding alcopops," Straw said in a statement. "I have asked George Howarth to look urgently with other ministers at the industry's own reaction to the problem."

"They will also consider what further action may be necessary to stop this abuse developing," he said. Bass Plc, brewers of Britain's best selling alcopop Hoochers Hooch, saw its shares slide 6p to 826p on the news.

"Alcopops abuse is a real concern. We all know the links between alcohol abuse and crime," said Straw. "Everything must be done to stop young people falling into a downward spiral of offending," he added.

The decision comes a day after alcopop makers were condemned as "grossly irresponsible" by a judge after he heard how a 14-year-old boy got drunk on alcoholic lemonade and cider, and then burned down a school.

Alcohol Concern welcomed the setting up of the ministerial group. Its director Eric Appleby said: "We have been concerned about the whole alcopops issue and the appeal of these drinks to under 18's since their introduction two years ago."

"For the first time we will get an independent and objective assessment of the issue. The drinks industry has set up a system of self-regulation, the Portman Group, which has not been successful first because it's voluntary and secondly because it's run and funded by the drinks industry itself."
Other alcopop brands include Two Dogs made by Merrydown and Whitbread's Vanilla Heist and Lemon Jag. Supermarkets also now have their own label brands like Sainsbury's Piranha.
Total alcopop sales are now worth 265 million pounds ($434.9 million) a year. ($ = 0.609 British Pounds)
